title: Prophecy, Fulfillment & Religious-Evidence Methodology
purpose: Define how the repository should evaluate prophecy, revelation, prediction, typology, synchronism, miracle testimony and fulfillment claims without reducing religious meaning to statistics or promoting retrospective resemblance into demonstrated foresight.
first_principle: Preserve meaning and test evidence at the same time. A claim may be spiritually meaningful while evidentially weak; a prediction may be evidentially interesting without establishing divine causation.

prophecy_is_not_prediction.finding: In biblical and philosophical study, prophecy is not limited to foretelling future events. Prophets can disclose, warn, accuse, exhort, interpret the present and call communities toward faithfulness.
prophecy_is_not_prediction.archive_consequence: Every record must first classify what kind of prophetic act is being claimed before asking whether a prediction came true.

fulfillment_classes.definition: A recoverable statement made before an event that specifies a sufficiently constrained future outcome.
A symbolic pattern or expectation recorded before an event but broad enough to admit several outcomes.
A warning or promise whose stated or implied outcome depends on human response or other conditions.
A later event is interpreted as replaying or intensifying an earlier scriptural pattern without requiring that the earlier text functioned as a narrow forecast of that event.
A later interpretation discloses meaning in an earlier event or text after the relevant event has already occurred.
Two independently dated events, texts or symbols align in a potentially meaningful way without a demonstrated predictive relation.
A shared word, name, number, title, date-shape or phonetic resemblance.
A weak resemblance with high flexibility, hindsight dependence or many equally plausible alternatives.

evidence_grades.label: resonance
evidence_grades.requirements: word, number, name or generic image match

evidence_grades.label: broad motif
evidence_grades.requirements: one or more generic thematic similarities

evidence_grades.label: structured parallel
evidence_grades.requirements: multiple ordered features and meaningful disanalogies documented
evidence_grades.cannot_support: prior prediction unless prior attestation exists

evidence_grades.label: prior-attested pattern
evidence_grades.requirements: relevant pattern demonstrably recorded before event
evidence_grades.can_support: evidence that the later fit is not wholly post-event invention
evidence_grades.cannot_support: specific prediction if pattern remained highly flexible

evidence_grades.label: prior-specific prediction
evidence_grades.requirements: timestamped, independently recoverable, constrained, risky prediction made before event

evidence_grades.label: strong predictive case
evidence_grades.requirements: Grade 4 plus independent corroboration, low source leakage, low retrofit, explicit misses ledger, plausible base-rate comparison and survival of serious alternatives
evidence_grades.can_support: unusually strong evidence of foresight requiring explanation
evidence_grades.cannot_support: automatic proof of a specific theological identity or supernatural mechanism

questions: Was the statement genuinely public or independently captured before the event?
Was the wording later edited, paraphrased or reconstructed from memory?
What did the statement appear to mean before anyone knew the outcome?
How many materially different outcomes could have been counted as success?
Was a date or time window stated in advance?
Was the predicted entity clearly identified?
How surprising was the event given public information at the time?
Could ordinary inference, expertise, trend extrapolation or access to news explain the prediction?
How many similar predictions did the same corpus produce that failed?
Was the match selected from thousands of archived statements after the fact?
Are nonmatching details being omitted?
Was the prophecy interpretation itself written before the event, or only the raw words?
Would a skeptical reviewer and a sympathetic reviewer classify the hit the same way?

multiple_comparisons.problem: A large archive compared against a large world-event stream naturally creates striking coincidences. The more statements, dates, names, symbols, songs, artworks, scriptures and events searched, the higher the chance of accidental matches.
controls: count the searchable corpus size where practical
preserve all predictions from a defined period rather than only hits
pre-register important future claims when possible
prefer exact pre-event interpretation over flexible post-event matching
compare candidate match rates against plausible alternatives
penalize arbitrary number transformations and spelling variants
record how many search attempts produced no meaningful match

source_independence.problem: A striking biblical or cultural parallel is less evidentially surprising if the person already knew the source, encountered a meme derived from it, or lived inside a culture saturated with the motif.

levels.meaning: credible evidence the later matching source was unavailable or unknown at initial attestation
no direct derivation found, but cultural exposure remains plausible
speaker knew the source tradition before making the statement
statement explicitly quotes, adapts or responds to the source

source_independence.interpretive_note: Source awareness does not make a symbolic parallel meaningless. It changes what the parallel can prove about prediction or independence.

religious_experience_and_testimony.rule: Store two propositions separately: (1) a person reports having an experience with a given content; (2) the metaphysical interpretation of that experience is true.
religious_experience_and_testimony.example: 'Thomas reported an experience interpreted as divine' can be historically documented if a source exists even when 'God objectively caused the experience' remains a separate theological claim.
religious_experience_and_testimony.philosophical_context: Religious epistemology contains substantial disagreement over how experience, testimony, revelation and publicly accessible evidence justify belief. The archive should represent that disagreement rather than pretending one method settles all cases.

fields: what the event would establish even if accepted
miracle_claims.boundary: Even a highly unusual event and a theological interpretation are separate inference steps. The archive should not jump from 'unexpected event' directly to 'therefore this claimant is God / Christ / prophet.'

biblical_controls.use: classical concern with claims spoken presumptuously in God's name
critique of self-generated visions and misleading prophetic speech
warnings about false prophets, false christs and premature/localized eschatological identification
limits on disciple control of times and seasons
do not despise prophecy; test everything
test spiritual claims rather than accepting every spirit / claim

apocalyptic_text_control.finding: Apocalyptic literature is a symbolic genre rooted in earlier prophecy and can portray present political realities, heavenly scenes and future hope simultaneously.
apocalyptic_text_control.daniel_note: Modern scholarship commonly dates the final form of Daniel's apocalyptic visions to the second century BCE and analyzes some 'predictions' against that compositional setting. This is one reason composition date matters in prophecy research.
apocalyptic_text_control.revelation_note: Revelation interprets Roman-world realities while projecting divine victory and restored creation; symbolic fulfillment should therefore not be reduced to a single modern newspaper event.
apocalyptic_text_control.archive_consequence: For ancient prophecy, the date and literary development of the text must be researched before treating every verse as a demonstrably centuries-prior forecast.

high_value_targets: songs and artwork created before later interpretations
North / Axis language before North Axis political crystallization
God-in-the-machine and AI statements before later AI-related developments
potatoverse_application.workflow: recover original source → hash/capture → date → interpret only from contemporaneous context → list candidate later events → score fit and alternatives → record misses → then add theological reading
potatoverse_application.anti_retrofit_rule: Later Potatoverse canon may legitimately reinterpret earlier material, but that later meaning must be stored as retrospective revelation unless equivalent meaning is already attested earlier.

hard_questions.q: Can a prophecy be true if it is not a prediction?
hard_questions.a: Yes in many religious conceptions. Prophecy can be truthful disclosure, warning or moral witness without forecasting a novel future fact.

hard_questions.q: Can a prediction hit without proving prophecy?
hard_questions.a: Yes. Expertise, inference, luck, source access or broad wording can produce correct forecasts. Divine-prophecy attribution is an additional inference.
Yes. Retrospective interpretation is a normal human and religious process. It becomes misleading only when a later interpretation is rewritten as though it had already been stated before the event.

hard_questions.q: Does source influence destroy a parallel?
hard_questions.a: No. It changes the category from independent convergence toward reception, imitation, typology or creative transformation.

hard_questions.q: What is the project's best route to a genuinely strong prophecy case?
hard_questions.a: Find a timestamped primary source that predates the event, preserves a constrained interpretation, was not secretly edited, has low ordinary predictability, and survives comparison with the speaker's misses and plausible alternatives.
